corrected_content.problem: Find the slope of the tangent at the point $(\sqrt{2}, 1)$ for the curve $x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 6$.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Implicit differentiation gives $2x+8y\,y'=0$, so $y'=-x/(4y)$ wherever $y\ne0$. At $(\sqrt2,1)$, the slope is $$-\frac{\sqrt2}{4}=-\frac1{2\sqrt2}.$$
